Theme

Latin word

mercēs

mercēs, mercēdis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

fee, charge (for work or a service); wages, rent; pay, wages, a fee; rent; pay, a fee; a reward; pay, wages; a fee; pay, wages (for work done)

In this lexicon

  • price

    also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.126: quī cum mercēde docēret; Phaedr. 1.8.12: et mercēdem postulēs

  • rate

    also used · classical · Sall. Cat. 37.7: manuum mercēde inopiam tolerāre (Lewis & Short)

  • rent

    the recommended word · classical · Caes. BC 3.21.1: mercēdēs habitātiōnum annuās conductōribus dōnāvit; Cic. Att. 12.32.2: mercēdēs Argīlētī et Aventīnī, the rents from (his houses in) the Argiletum and on the Aventine; Traupman 370: mercēdem huic cellae dare, to pay the rent for this room

  • reward

    also used · classical · Phaedr. 1.8.12; Cic. Div. 1.92 (Lewis & Short)

  • salary

    also used · classical · Traupman 373: aequam mercēdem alicui solvere, to pay someone a fair salary; M-O s.v. salary, pay (of employees), wages

  • wage

    the recommended word · classical · Sall. Cat. 37.7: manuum mercēde inopiam tolerāverat, had kept poverty off with the wages of their hands; Traupman 403: mercēdem accipere, to receive wages; mercēdem tribuere, to pay wages; M-O s.v. salary, pay (of employees), wages

Examples

  • Sūmptus ūnīus generis objectus est, habitātiōnis; trīgintā mīlibus dīxistis eum habitāre. Nunc dēmum intellegō P. Clōdī īnsulam esse vēnālem, cujus hic in aediculīs habitat decem, ut opīnor, mīlibus.

    Only one kind of spending has been laid against him, his rent: you said he paid thirty thousand. Now at last I understand that Publius Clodius’s block of flats is up for sale: he lives in a little flat in it for ten thousand, I believe.Cic. Cael. 17
